'''Hiroshi Enatsu''' (12 September 1922  – 4 August 2019) was a Japanese [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] who contributed to a [[special relativity|relativistic]] [[Hamiltonian mechanics|Hamiltonian formalism]] in [[quantum field theory]].

== Academic works ==
Enatsu has found<ref>[[Matej Pavšič]], [http://www-f1.ijs.si/~pavsic/Book1Corr.pdf  "The Landscape of Theoretical Physics: A Global View, From Point Particles to the Brane World and Beyond, in Search of a Unifying Principle", Kluwer Academic, 2001]</ref> that the [[Canonical commutation relation|commutation relation]]<ref>[https://academic.oup.com/ptp/article/30/2/236/1868993 Relativistic Hamiltonian Formalism in Quantum Field Theory and Micro-Noncausality, August 1963]</ref>

<math>[\psi (x, \tau), \psi ^*(x', \tau)] = \delta ( x - x' )</math>

in a relativistic Hamiltonian formalism  
is equivalent to that in the conventional non-relativistic Hamiltonian formalism of quantum field theory, 
where <math>[\psi, \phi] = \psi \phi - \phi \psi</math> is the [[commutator]], 
<math> x </math> is [[spacetime|space-time]] coordinates, 
<math>\tau</math> is [[proper time]], 
<math>\psi ^*</math> is [[Hermitian adjoint]] of <math>\psi</math>, 
and <math>\delta (x)</math> is the [[Dirac delta function]], 
with the aid of the relation

<math>\epsilon ( x - x' ) \epsilon ( \tau - \tau' )=1</math>.

Here, 
a [[step function]] <math>\epsilon ( x ) </math> follows <math>\epsilon ( x )=1</math> for <math> 0 < x </math>, 
and <math>\epsilon ( x )=-1</math> for <math>x <  0</math>.

==Biography==
===Early stage===
Enatsu was born on 12 September 1922 in [[Miyakonojō]] as a son of Eizo and Fumi (Kuroiwa) Enatsu.  
Miyakonojō is a town within the territory of the former [[Satsuma Domain]], 
and it was rather natural for Enatsu to receive an education in [[Kagoshima]]. 
So, he spent in Kagoshima for secondary education and [[junior college]].

===Encounter with Hideki Yukawa===
In the last year of junior college, 
Hideki Yukawa made a lecture on meson theory at Kagoshima. 
After listening to the lecture, 
Enatsu became interested in Yukawa and meson theory,
so he decided to study under Yukawa.  
He studied on meson theory under Yukawa in undergraduate course.  
He received Bachelor of Science from [[Kyoto University|Kyoto Imperial University]] in 1944.  
He received [[Doctor of Science]].<ref>[https://translate.google.co.jp/translate?hl=en&sl=ja&u=http://hakase.site/article/29086&prev=search Doctoral dissertation on nucleon self-energy and mass spectrum of elementary particles ]</ref> from [[Kyoto University|Kyoto Imperial University]] in 1953 under Yukawa.
Enatsu was an assistant under Yukawa at Kyoto University<ref>[https://translate.googleusercontent.com/translate_c?depth=1&hl=en&prev=search&rurl=translate.google.co.jp&sl=ja&sp=nmt4&u=https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/soken/3/4/3_KJ00004821908/_article/-char/ja/&xid=17259,15700022,15700186,15700191,15700256,15700259,15700262,15700265,15700271,15700283&usg=ALkJrhh5LDxnsFGDxUAXj4rD6yVQ0sUvhQ Prof. Yukawa to Hiroshi Enatsu (Overseas News)]</ref><ref>[https://translate.google.co.jp/translate?hl=en&sl=ja&u=https://ci.nii.ac.jp/naid/110006550361&prev=search Prof. Yukawa to Hiroshi Enatsu (Overseas News)]</ref> from 1946 to 1957.  
Enatsu was a research assistant at Columbia University <ref>[https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.95.263 Theory of Unstable Heavy Particles, received May 1953, published July 1954]</ref> in New York City from 1952 to 1953.

===Encounter with Niels Bohr===
Enatsu was a visiting member of the Institute for Theoretical Physics in Copenhagen<ref>[http://archon.nbi.dk/?p=digitallibrary/digitalcontent&id=5413 Niels Bohr Private Correspondence]</ref><ref>[http://archon.nbi.dk/?p=digitallibrary/digitalcontent&id=5414 Niels Bohr Private Correspondence]</ref> from 1955 to 1956.  
During his stay in Copenhagen, 
he could ask some questions to Bohr almost every week.
It was a special treatment.

===Professor at Ritsumeikan University===
In 1957, 
Enatsu was an assistant professor and inaugurated a professor at [[Ritsumeikan University]] in Kyoto.  
From 1971 to 1972, 
he was also the dean of faculty of science and engineering at Ritsumeikan University.  
In 1988, 
he retired from a professor at Ritsumeikan University in Kyoto, and has been a professor emeritus.  
In 1997. 
he received the 3rd class of the [[Order of the Sacred Treasure]].  
Enatsu died on 4 August 2019 in Kyoto<ref>[https://translate.google.co.jp/translate?hl=en&sl=ja&u=https://www.subutsu.com/%3Fp%3D476&prev=search Intelligence: Dr. Hiroshi Enatsu]</ref>
